result.title: Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are becoming general readers of medical images, yet they remain weak at locating small abnormalities. Brain metastases expose this gap: at 384 px a 0.1 mL lesion covers less than a quarter of one visual token, and at one false positive per scan frontier MLLMs find fewer than 30% of lesions of 0.1-1 mL. Fine-tuning on one dataset helps but transfers poorly, and improving it further is slow trial and error steered by a single score. We introduce LANTERN (Lesion-finding AgeNt Through Error-driven Recursive learNing), a framework in which an MLLM improves recursively from its own misses. LANTERN recasts model development as an error-driven loop: a failure census attributes every missed lesion to one of four causes, an LLM mentor revises one of four levels (evidence acquisition, visual representation, learning policy, decision aggregation) per round, and a rule frozen before the first round decides what is kept, without test data and with every tool call audited. Over 15 unattended rounds, LANTERN raises a fine-tuned 4B MLLM from finding 75% to 94% of lesions at one false positive per scan on BraTS-MET, and 91% of those of 0.1-1 mL, compared with at most 51% and 29% for five frontier MLLMs read under the starting protocol; the gains hold on an external cohort (89%) and on unseen meningiomas (77%). These results show that an MLLM's own misses, attributed to their causes, can drive its reliable recursive self-improvement.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对 MLLM 难以定位极小脑转移灶的问题（0.1 mL 病灶不足四分之一个视觉 token），提出 LANTERN：将模型开发变成由自身漏检驱动的循环，先对漏检做四类归因，再由 LLM mentor 每轮修改证据获取、视觉表示、学习策略或决策聚合中的一层，并按预先冻结的规则保留改动。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉 token 容量限制 + 漏检归因 + 分级修改证据获取与视觉表示」直接对应 LVR 中对视觉细节是否进入内部状态、证据筛选与监督分配的关切，可供核查细粒度视觉信息在表示层面丢失的诊断方式。
